sections.normalized_html: The greatest possible value of [MATH: u] is [MATH: 12] less than [MATH: 5] times another number [MATH: v.] Which inequality represents the possible values of [MATH: u?]
sections.readable_text: The greatest possible value of [MATH: u] is [MATH: 12] less than [MATH: 5] times another number [MATH: v.] Which inequality represents the possible values of [MATH: u?]

sections.normalized_html:
The phrase “the greatest possible value of [MATH: u] is [MATH: 12] less than [MATH: 5] times the value of [MATH: v]” can be unpacked in parts to understand how it translates to an inequality.

  • First, the expression “[MATH: 5] times the value of [MATH: v]” means we compute [MATH: 5v.]

  • Next, the phrase “[MATH: 12] less than [MATH: 5v]” tells us to subtract [MATH: 12] from that result, giving [MATH: 5v - 12.]

  • Then, the phrase “greatest possible value” means that [MATH: u] must be less than or equal to this amount.

Putting these pieces together, we get the inequality: [MATH: u \leq 5v - 12]

sections.normalized_html:
The phrase “[MATH: m] is not greater than [MATH: 9] less than [MATH: 5] times the value of [MATH: n]” can be unpacked in parts to understand how it translates to an inequality.

  • First, the expression “[MATH: 5] times the value of [MATH: n]” means we compute [MATH: 5n.]

  • Next, the phrase “[MATH: 9] less than [MATH: 5n]” tells us to subtract [MATH: 9] from that result, giving [MATH: 5n - 9.]

  • Then, the phrase “not greater than” means that [MATH: m] must be less than or equal to this amount.

Putting these pieces together, we get the inequality: [MATH: m \leq 5n - 9]

Substituting [MATH: n = 4] into the inequality yields [MATH: m|≤ 5(4) − 9; m|≤ 20 − 9; m|≤ 11.]

So, the maximum possible value of [MATH: m] is [MATH: \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{11}.]

Item 2 — Example: Finding an Equivalent Inequality
